headline: Romualdez Transferred to PGH for Court-Ordered Independent Medical Assessment
seoTitle: Romualdez Transferred to PGH for Independent Medical Assessment | FMB News
seoDescription: Martin Romualdez was transferred to Philippine General Hospital for a court-ordered independent medical assessment as the Sandiganbayan weighs his hospital-confinement request.
deck: The former House speaker was received at Philippine General Hospital under a Sandiganbayan order, with an independent medical assessment now set to guide the court's next decision on his detention.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ombudsman Files Plunder Case Against Martin Romualdez Over Alleged Flood-Control Kickback Scheme
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported the Ombudsman filing, the Sandiganbayan ordered Romualdez arrested, later designated New Quezon City Jail as his detention facility, and has now ordered his transfer to Philippine General Hospital for an independent medical assessment before deciding whether continued medical confinement is warranted.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Former House Speaker and Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez was transferred from Cardinal Santos Medical Center to the Philippine General Hospital in Manila on September 12 for an independent medical assessment ordered by the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology said PGH received Romualdez at approximately 8:45 a.m. pursuant to the court order. The BJMP said PGH would submit findings and recommendations to the Sandiganbayan and that the bureau would await further court instructions before implementing any transfer to the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas.

GMA News, ABS-CBN News, Inquirer.net and Philstar.com separately reported the transfer and assessment process. The development follows the Sandiganbayan's earlier commitment order designating the Quezon City jail as Romualdez's detention facility while his request for continued hospital confinement remained unresolved.
This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's first report
paragraphs: FMB News first reported on September 7 that the Office of the Ombudsman had filed a plunder case against Romualdez and three co-accused. Later developments included an arrest warrant and a September 10 commitment order designating New Quezon City Jail as his detention facility.

The material new development is that Romualdez has now physically left the private hospital and entered PGH for the independent medical assessment ordered by the court. The assessment will help determine whether continued hospital confinement is medically justified or whether the court will direct his transfer to the jail facility already designated for his detention.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Romualdez is facing a plunder charge arising from allegations tied to flood-control and other government infrastructure projects. Prosecutors allege that he and co-accused received at least ₱7.44 billion in commissions, kickbacks and other benefits. Those allegations remain unproven, and the court has not found Romualdez guilty of the criminal charge.

Romualdez's doctors have cited health concerns in support of his request to remain in a medical facility. The Sandiganbayan sought an independent assessment from PGH rather than relying only on the private medical evaluation already submitted to the court.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The case concerns allegations involving billions of pesos in public infrastructure spending, including flood-control projects, and has become a major test of accountability for high-ranking officials accused of corruption.

The PGH assessment also matters because it bears directly on how the justice system handles medical-confinement requests by high-profile detainees. The key legal distinction remains unchanged: decisions about custody or medical treatment do not establish guilt or innocence in the underlying plunder case.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: PGH's final medical findings and recommendations were not yet public in the reporting reviewed by FMB News.

The Sandiganbayan had not yet issued a final ruling on whether Romualdez may remain confined in a hospital or must be transferred to the Quezon City jail facility designated in the earlier commitment order.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next material development will be PGH's independent assessment and the Sandiganbayan's resulting custody order. The court had directed PGH to submit its assessment by September 13, with a representative expected to present it to the court the following day, according to GMA News.
FMB News will also watch the scheduled arraignment and any further court orders, official BJMP custody updates, or filings from the prosecution and defense that materially change the case.

verificationNotes: The central event is verified by GMA News, ABS-CBN News, Inquirer.net and Philstar.com, which separately reported Romualdez's September 12 transfer to PGH.
GMA News reported a direct BJMP statement confirming that PGH received Romualdez at approximately 8:45 a.m. pursuant to the Sandiganbayan order.
The article distinguishes the court-ordered medical assessment and custody process from any determination of guilt in the underlying plunder case.
The ₱7.44-billion figure is identified as an allegation in the prosecution case, not as a judicially established loss or proven ill-gotten wealth.

This is a material continuation of FMB News' September 7 first report. The visible Continues from link points to that earliest relevant canonical FMB News article, while the September 11 commitment-order continuation remains intact.
The unresolved questions are explicitly disclosed: PGH's final findings and the Sandiganbayan's next custody order were not yet public at the time of publication.
